title: Jailer 2 Opens Near ₹125 Crore Worldwide as Rajinikanth Tops His Own Record
excerpt: Sacnilk figures put the India gross at ₹121.43 crore on day one, with a record Telugu-states opening for a Tamil film and the third-biggest Hindi-dubbed Kollywood debut.
body:
• Jailer 2 collected about ₹125 crore worldwide on its first day, with India gross at ₹121.43 crore and net at ₹101.93 crore, according to Sacnilk figures reported by Koimoi.
  • Tamil Nadu led with ₹29.60 crore gross, and the Telugu states delivered ₹21.86 crore — a record opening there for a Tamil film.
  • The Hindi version earned ₹4.06 crore net, the third-biggest opening for a Hindi-dubbed Kollywood film after Leo and the first Jailer.
  • With a reported budget of ₹425–450 crore, the sequel needs a long run — but near-full houses in Chennai (97% occupancy) point to a big first weekend.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has opened to about ₹125 crore worldwide on its first day, according to GreatAndhra, as the sequel outpaced the opening of the original film and set records in the Telugu states. Sacnilk's day-one tally, reported by Koimoi, puts the India gross at ₹121.43 crore and the net at ₹101.93 crore, making it one of the biggest openings ever for an Indian film.

The numbers confirm what the advance sales had promised. The film had already banked ₹38 crore in advance bookings before release, and fans from Chennai to Japan and Dubai turned the opening into a festival of first-day-first-show celebrations.

"A Record in Hindi Too The Hindi-dubbed version, titled Rajini The Jailer 2, collected ₹4.06 crore net on day one."

Where the Money Came From

Tamil Nadu was the engine, contributing ₹29.60 crore gross. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana followed with ₹21.86 crore gross — the biggest opening ever recorded in the Telugu states for a Tamil film, ahead of the mark set by Jailer in 2023, according to Koimoi's Sacnilk-based report. Karnataka added ₹11.30 crore, Kerala ₹6.55 crore, and the rest of India ₹7.28 crore.

https://x.com/smileyboyoff/status/2110587031747461274

Occupancy built through the day in Tamil Nadu: 82.12% for morning shows, 84.85% in the afternoon and 87.60% by the evening, Sacnilk reported. Chennai theatres ran at 97% and Trichy at 95%, the kind of figures usually reserved for a festival release.

A Record in Hindi Too

The Hindi-dubbed version, titled Rajini The Jailer 2, collected ₹4.06 crore net on day one. Koimoi ranks that as the third-biggest Hindi opening for a Kollywood film, behind Leo (₹7.3 crore) and the original Jailer (₹5.95 crore), and ahead of 2.0 (₹3.9 crore) and Kabali (₹3.65 crore). For a sequel whose core market is Tamil, a top-three dubbed opening widens its runway in the north Indian multiplexes where the first film built a steady audience.

What the Opening Has to Beat

The scale comes with scale-sized expectations. Pinkvilla, cited by GreatAndhra, has reported a production budget of ₹425–450 crore, which means the film likely needs a worldwide run well past ₹1,000 crore to be counted an unqualified success — the target the makers were chasing even before release. The first Jailer opened at ₹78.60 crore in India in 2023 on its way to a blockbuster run; the sequel has cleared that opening by a wide margin.

Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar and produced by Sun Pictures, Jailer 2 brings back Rajinikanth as Muthuvel Pandian, with Mohanlal and Shiva Rajkumar returning and a cameo that has already set up a third instalment. Trade watchers will now look at the Saturday and Sunday numbers: openings this size usually hold if family audiences, not just fans, turn up on day two and three.

What's Next

The first weekend total, due by Monday, will show whether Jailer 2 is tracking toward the ₹1,000-crore club or settling into a strong-but-front-loaded run. Either way, day one has already done its job: this is the biggest opening of Rajinikanth's career, delivered at 75, in his fifth decade as a star.
